# Comprehensive Learning Guide: Implementing MVC ToDo App with PHP Laravel

## Course Overview

This intermediate-level course teaches you how to build a fully functional **Model-View-Controller (MVC) ToDo application** using **Laravel**, one of the most popular and interview-friendly PHP frameworks. The course spans **82 practice tasks** and covers everything from project setup through deployment, with emphasis on real-world architectural patterns, database design, and RESTful API principles.

**Who it's for:**
- Mid-level PHP developers transitioning to Laravel
- Full-stack developers preparing for tech interviews
- Backend engineers wanting to master modern PHP frameworks
- Anyone building portfolio projects for job applications

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
- Laravel is used by thousands of companies globally (Twitter, Netflix, Slack all use or have used Laravel-based services)
- MVC architecture understanding is fundamental to nearly all web frameworks
- Demonstrates ability to work with routing, middleware, authentication, and database design
- Real application-building skills trump algorithm knowledge in many mid-level roles
- Provides portfolio evidence beyond coding challenges

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Laravel Framework Fundamentals** – Project structure, service providers, configuration, and artisan CLI
- **Routing & HTTP Controllers** – RESTful route design, request/response handling, form validation
- **Model-View Architecture** – Eloquent ORM, query builders, relationships, and database migrations
- **Blade Templating Engine** – Layouts, components, directives, and dynamic content rendering
- **Authentication & Authorization** – User registration, login, middleware, policies, and role-based access control
- **Database Design & Migrations** – Schema design, indexes, relationships, and data integrity constraints
- **API Development** – JSON responses, resource controllers, error handling, and versioning
- **Testing & Debugging** – Unit tests, feature tests, PHPUnit, and Laravel's testing utilities

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundation & Setup (Tasks 1–12)**
1. Install Laravel and set up development environment
2. Understand project structure (app/, routes/, resources/, database/)
3. Configure .env and database connections
4. Learn artisan commands (make:model, make:controller, migrate)
5. Set up Git and version control
6. Create initial database schema for ToDos
7. Understand service container and dependency injection basics
8. Configure local database (SQLite/MySQL)
9. Run first migration
10. Explore tinker REPL for model testing
11. Set up IDE helpers and autocompletion
12. Review Laravel documentation structure

### **Phase 2: Models & Database (Tasks 13–25)**
13. Create Todo Eloquent model with properties and attributes
14. Write initial migration for todos table
15. Understand timestamps and soft deletes
16. Create User model and authentication scaffolding
17. Define Model relationships (User hasMany Todos)
18. Write migration for users table
19. Create query scopes (scopeIncomplete, scopeByUser)
20. Implement accessors and mutators
21. Add fillable mass-assignment properties
22. Write database seeders for test data
23. Create factories for model testing
24. Understand N+1 query problem and eager loading
25. Implement query optimization with select()

### **Phase 3: Routing & Controllers (Tasks 26–38)**
26. Set up RESTful routes for ToDo resource
27. Create TodoController with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy
28. Implement request validation in controller
29. Create form requests (StoreTodoRequest, UpdateTodoRequest)
30. Handle route model binding
31. Implement soft deletes and restore functionality
32. Add pagination to index view
33. Create redirect responses with session flashing
34. Implement query filtering (by status, due date)
35. Add sorting capabilities to index
36. Create UserController for user management
37. Implement authorization checks (can user edit this todo?)
38. Handle 404 and 403 error responses

### **Phase 4: Views & Templating (Tasks 39–50)**
39. Create base Blade layout with navigation
40. Build todo index template with iteration
41. Implement create/edit form templates (reusable partials)
42. Add CSRF token to forms
43. Render validation errors in forms
44. Create todo detail/show view
45. Implement pagination links
46. Add flash message display (success, error alerts)
47. Use Blade directives (@if, @foreach, @auth, @guest)
48. Create form components for DRY form handling
49. Implement search and filter UI
50. Add dynamic styling based on todo status

### **Phase 5: Authentication & Authorization (Tasks 51–60)**
51. Implement user registration with validation
52. Create login functionality
53. Set up password hashing and verification
54. Implement remember-me functionality
55. Create logout action
56. Build password reset flow (email tokens)
57. Create authorization policies for todos
58. Implement middleware for auth checks
59. Add role-based access control (admin vs user)
60. Protect routes with auth middleware

### **Phase 6: API & Advanced Features (Tasks 61–72)**
61. Create API routes separate from web routes
62. Build JSON resource classes for todos
63. Implement API authentication (token/sanctum)
64. Create API endpoints (GET /api/todos, POST /api/todos)
65. Add pagination and filtering to API
66. Implement proper HTTP status codes
67. Create API error response formatting
68. Add API rate limiting
69. Document API endpoints with comments
70. Implement bulk operations (multiple delete)
71. Add todo priority and tags features
72. Implement due date reminders/notifications

### **Phase 7: Testing & Deployment (Tasks 73–82)**
73. Write unit tests for Todo model
74. Create feature tests for controller actions
75. Test authentication flows
76. Test authorization policies
77. Test validation rules
78. Implement test database seeding
79. Run test coverage analysis
80. Deploy to shared hosting or cloud (Heroku/DigitalOcean)
81. Set up environment variables for production
82. Monitor logs and performance; create deployment checklist

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Architecture & Design Patterns**
- MVC separation of concerns
- Repository pattern (optional advanced)
- Service classes for business logic
- Dependency injection and IoC container usage
- SOLID principles application

### **Database Mastery**
- Schema design and normalization
- Foreign key relationships
- Query optimization and eager loading
- Migrations and rollbacks
- Database transactions

### **Request/Response Handling**
- Form validation (both frontend and backend)
- Request objects and custom requests
- Response formatting (HTML/JSON)
- Middleware pipeline understanding
- Error handling and exception catching

### **Modern PHP Practices**
- Namespacing and autoloading (PSR-4)
- Object-oriented design
- Traits and composition
- Static methods vs instance methods
- Type hinting and return types

### **Frontend Integration**
- Server-side templating (Blade)
- Form handling with CSRF protection
- Session management
- Cookie handling
- Asset pipeline (CSS/JS bundling)

### **Testing & Quality**
- Unit and feature testing with PHPUnit
- Test-driven development mindset
- Mocking and assertions
- Code coverage analysis

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: CRUD Operations with Relationships**

**Description:** Implement a complete todo creation flow where a user can create a todo, assign it to a category, and view it in a list filtered by category.

**Tasks involved:**
- Create Category model and migration
- Define hasMany relationship between User→Todo and Category
- Build form validation
- Implement index with filtering
- Test authorization

**Code sketch:**

```php
// Model relationship (app/Models/Todo.php)
class Todo extends Model {
    public function user() {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class);
    }
    
    public function category() {
        return $this->belongsTo(Category::class);
    }
    
    public function scopeByCategory($query, $categoryId) {
        return $query->where('category_id', $categoryId);
    }
}
